'''Statistics Denmark''' ({{langx|da|'''Danmarks Statistik'''}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Om Danmarks Statistik|url=https://www.dst.dk/da/OmDS|access-date=2021-08-04|website=www.dst.dk|language=da|archive-date=2021-07-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728064926/https://www.dst.dk/da/OmDS|url-status=live}}</ref>) is a [[Denmark|Danish]] governmental organization under the Ministry of Digital Affairs, reporting to the Minister for Digital Affairs. The organization is responsible for creating [[statistics]] on the Danish society,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=About us|url=https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140526230013/https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS|archive-date=26 May 2014|access-date=4 August 2021|website=www.dst.dk|language=en}}</ref> including [[employment]] statistics, [[trade balance]], and [[demographics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Organisation chart |url=https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS/organisation/organisationsdiagram |access-date=2023-08-13 |website=www.dst.dk |language=en |archive-date=2023-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608192801/https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS/organisation/organisationsdiagram |url-status=live }}</ref>

Statistics Denmark relies heavily on public registers for statistical production, with a particular emphasis on the [[Personal identification number (Denmark)|Central Person Register]] for population statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Population: Accuracy and reliability |url=https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/dokumentation/documentationofstatistics/the-population/accuracy-and-reliability |access-date=2023-08-15 |website=www.dst.dk |language=en}}</ref>

Statistics Denmark's electronic data bank ('''Statbank.dk''') is available freely in Danish or English to any user.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=StatBank Denmark |url=https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/brug-statistikken/muligheder-i-statistikbanken |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804005842/https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/brug-statistikken/muligheder-i-statistikbanken |archive-date=4 August 2021 |access-date=4 August 2021 |website=www.dst.dk |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=StatBank Denmark |url=https://www.statbank.dk/statbank5a/default.asp?w=1440 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304181844/http://statbank.dk/statbank5a/default.asp?w=1440 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |access-date=2021-08-04 |website=www.statbank.dk |language=da}}</ref> It contains nearly all in-house produced statistics, which can be presented as cross-tables, diagrams, or maps, and can be exported to other programs for further analysis.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=StatBank Denmark |url=https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/brug-statistikken/muligheder-i-statistikbanken |access-date=2023-08-13 |website=www.dst.dk |language=en |archive-date=2021-08-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804005842/https://www.dst.dk/en/Statistik/brug-statistikken/muligheder-i-statistikbanken |url-status=live }}</ref> When new general statistics are published in News from Statistics Denmark, the same data is simultaneously released in a more detailed format through the data bank.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board |url=https://dsbb.imf.org/sddsplus/dqaf-base/country/DNK/category/POP00 |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=dsbb.imf.org}}</ref>

== History ==

The first population census in Denmark was conducted in 1769.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Statistics Denmark|url=https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/Udgivelser/GetPubFile.aspx?id=4583&sid=statistics_denmark|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804005335/https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/Udgivelser/GetPubFile.aspx?id=4583&sid=statistics_denmark|archive-date=4 August 2021|access-date=4 August 2021|website=www.dst.dk|format=PDF}}</ref> Statistics Denmark was founded in January 1850, following the introduction of democracy to Denmark,<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=DNSS Document: Country Profile of Denmark |url=https://unstats.un.org/unsd/dnss/print.aspx?docID=505 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221103045128/http://unstats.un.org/unsd/dnss/print.aspx?docID=505 |archive-date=2022-11-03 |access-date=2021-08-04 |website=unstats.un.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Statistics Denmark |url=https://unstats.un.org/unsd/dnss/docViewer.aspx?docID=2758}}</ref> under the name "Statistical Bureau."<ref name=":5" />

In 1966, the [[Danish Parliament]] adopted the Act on Statistics Denmark. This act changed the name of the Statistical Bureau to Statistics Denmark and granted an independent Board of Directors the responsibility to determine the institution's work program. This allowed Statistics Denmark to operate independently from government control.<ref name=":0">{{Cite act|date=2018|title=Act on Statistics Denmark 2018|url=https://www.dst.dk/Site/Dst/SingleFiles/GetArchiveFile.aspx?fi=1424585935&fo=0&ext=direktion}}</ref>

The Act also provides grants Statistics Denmark with access to the basic data necessary for it to produce its statistics. Under the Act, public authorities are required to supply the information they possess when it is requested by Statistics Denmark.<ref name=":0" /> The private sector is also obligated to provide certain information.

Since 1970, censuses have been exclusively based on administrative registers, with private citizens only participating in surveys on a voluntary basis only. In line with these principles, Statistics Denmark has focused to develop a data collection system primary relent on the administrative registers of other public offices. Other collection methods are employed when necessary but are considered as supplementary.<ref name=":6" />

==Role of Statistics Denmark==
The production of statistics in Denmark is highly centralized, with Statistics Denmark as at its center.<ref name=":4" /> Therefore, the organization responsible for providing reliable data to the citizenry, politicians, the business community, public agencies, news media, educational institutions, researchers, and the [[European Union|EU]].<ref name=":4" />

The overall mission of the institution is stated in its ''Strategy 2005'' paper as follows:<ref name=":4" />

{{Blockquote|text="Our mission is to produce and disseminate all trustworthy statistics on social and economic trends in society, which are an essential condition for its democracy and economy to work."}}

Statistics Denmark also offers "customized solutions" for purchase. These are tailor-made statistical reports focusing on a specific region and/or form of activity not included in the organization's standard products.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Customized solutions |url=https://www.dst.dk/en/TilSalg/skraeddersyede-loesninger |access-date=2023-08-13 |website=www.dst.dk |language=en |archive-date=2023-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608083541/https://www.dst.dk/en/TilSalg/skraeddersyede-loesninger |url-status=live }}</ref>

==International Cooperation==
Statistics Denmark actively participates in international statistical activities, including its involvement in the joint European statistical program.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESS – European Statistical System|url=https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS/strategi-og-kvalitet/internationalt-samarbejde/ess|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151023184753/https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS/strategi-og-kvalitet/internationalt-samarbejde/ess|archive-date=23 October 2015|access-date=4 August 2021|website=www.dst.dk|language=en}}</ref>

As a member of the EU, Denmark participates in a binding agreement regarding the compilation, preparation, and dissemination of statistics. While the requirements for statistical output align, to some extent, with Denmark's national needs, significant resources are devoted to fulfilling of Danish obligations.{{Citation needed|date=August 2021}}

Statistics Denmark is also actively engaged in international organizations such as the [[United Nations Statistical Commission]], the [[Conference of European Statisticians]] (CES), the [[Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development|Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development]], the [[International Monetary Fund]], and the [[ILO|International Labour Organization]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cooperation with other international organizations|url=https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS/strategi-og-kvalitet/internationalt-samarbejde/samarbejde-med-andre-internationale-organisationer|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151023183834/https://www.dst.dk/en/OmDS/strategi-og-kvalitet/internationalt-samarbejde/samarbejde-med-andre-internationale-organisationer|archive-date=23 October 2015|access-date=4 August 2021|website=www.dst.dk|language=en}}</ref>

==Consulting abroad==

Statistics Denmark has an International Consulting division that offers assistance to sister agencies in various countries outside the EU. This division aims to help these organizations improve their capacity to produce reliable, useful, and accessible national statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Consulting abroad |url=https://www.dst.dk/en/consulting |access-date=2023-08-13 |website=www.dst.dk |language=en |archive-date=2023-06-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230610204219/https://www.dst.dk/en/consulting |url-status=live }}</ref>
